title: BCCI Schedules August Review of India's UK Tour Collapse as Staff Exits Loom
excerpt: The board will examine India's unprecedented five-match T20I losing streak and 1-2 ODI series defeat in England, with assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate requesting release and fielding coach T Dilip under scrutiny.
body:
• The BCCI will conduct a comprehensive review in August covering India's white-ball performances in Ireland, England, and Zimbabwe, with the exact date yet to be confirmed.
  • India lost five consecutive T20Is for the first time in history — a 2-0 defeat to Ireland followed by a 4-1 loss to England — under new captain Shreyas Iyer, who is winless in six games as skipper.
  • Assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate has requested release from his contract, and fielding coach T Dilip faces scrutiny over India's poor catching and ground fielding during the UK tour.
  • The review comes just months after India won the T20 World Cup at home in March under the previous captain.

The Board of Control for Cricket in India will hold a review meeting in August to examine the Indian team's dismal white-ball performances across the UK, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia confirmed. The review will cover matches in Ireland, England, and Zimbabwe, and will also address the future of support staff under head coach Gautam Gambhir.

The Scale of the Collapse

India suffered their first-ever bilateral series defeat to Ireland in Belfast before traveling to England, where the problems deepened. Harry Brook's England side handed India a 4-1 thrashing in the five-match T20I series, including a nine-wicket demolition in Bristol where Brook smashed an unbeaten 79 off 35 balls.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=h7liJWNijcM

The defeats marked the first time in Indian cricket history that the men's team lost five consecutive T20 internationals. In the three-match ODI series that followed, India managed only one win, losing the series 1-2. The solitary bright spot came in Zimbabwe, where India won a T20I series as expected against weaker opposition.

The speed of the turnaround is striking. India lifted the T20 World Cup on home soil in March, their second consecutive title. Within four months, the defending champions were being outplayed in all conditions outside the subcontinent.

The Captain's Record

Shreyas Iyer replaced Suryakumar Yadav as T20I captain after the World Cup and has yet to win a match in the format. Of six games under his leadership, India have lost five with one abandoned. His broader record is worse: he has lost nine of his last ten completed T20Is as captain, a run stretching back into the IPL.

The much-anticipated international debut of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, the IPL Orange Cap winner, produced scores of 14, 13, and 15 in his first three matches — a return that underlined the batting group's inability to adapt to English conditions.

Staff Under the Microscope

The review will extend beyond player performance. Assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate, who completed his initial two-year contract, has asked the BCCI to relieve him of his duties. His request is expected to be accepted.

"We will hold the review meeting in August. It will cover all the white-ball matches in recent times, particularly those in Ireland and England."

— Devajit Saikia, BCCI Secretary

Fielding coach T Dilip faces sharper scrutiny. India's catching and ground fielding were below par throughout the UK tour, with dropped chances proving costly in several matches. There is no immediate clarity on whether Dilip's contract will be renewed or terminated following the review.

The Bigger Question

Saikia described the slump as a "purely bad phase" and said the BCCI considers the poor results within the range of what can happen in international cricket. But the pattern raises structural questions about how India prepare for overseas conditions, particularly in formats where adaptability is critical.

Head coach Gambhir was not singled out by name, but the review will inevitably touch on tactical decisions that backfired during the England series — including playing three spinners in conditions favoring pace and choosing to bat first on surfaces that offered early movement.

The review meeting will also coincide with squad selection for the away Test series against Sri Lanka, with two Tests scheduled in Galle and Colombo from August 15 to 27. Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj are likely to return to the Test squad, while all-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy remains doubtful due to a quadriceps injury.

For Indian cricket, the August review represents a fork in the road: acknowledge systemic gaps in overseas preparation, or file the results under bad luck and move on. The answer will shape the team's trajectory heading into a packed international calendar.
nri_angle: The review will be closely watched by cricket fans across the diaspora, many of whom traveled to UK venues to watch the defending world champions lose five consecutive T20Is — a first in Indian cricket history.
